commit.message:
ci: fix path-filter quantifier so docs-only PRs skip unit tests (#2545)

dorny/paths-filter defaults to the `some` predicate, under which a negated
pattern (`!pandera/api/pandas/**`, ...) is compiled to an *inverted* matcher.
That matcher returns true for any file *not* in the excluded directory, so the
`common` filter in .github/filters.yaml — a mix of 2 positives and 60+
negations — matched essentially every changed file. The result: a docs-only PR
(say, `docs/source/conf.py`) classified as `common=true`, which forced every
test area to run.

Switch the filter to `some-with-excludes`, the semantics the `common` filter's
include/exclude design assumes: a file matches only when it hits a positive
pattern and none of the negations. Positive-only filters (`docs`, `global`,
per-backend) are unaffected. Docs-only PRs now trigger only the docs job, and
shared-code changes (e.g. `pandera/api/base/**`) still run every area.
